title: Staunlabor: where the load goes
description: Cloud Run, Cloud SQL and the backend's per-route log metrics, one row per bottleneck (deploy/grafana/README.md).

options.content:
**Which is it?** Each row below answers one question. Read them top to bottom while a post brings visitors.

1. **CPU** — backend CPU near 100 % *and* time in the app far above the CPU per call: requests wait for the one core. The route panels say whose calculation it is.
2. **Cold starts** — new instances, startup latency and *pending* latency rise together; cold requests show which route paid the first-time work.
3. **The budget** — 429s marked *refused by the budget* rise while CPU is fine: visitors share an address (an office, a proxy). The line names no address, so this cannot tell one busy visitor from many behind one.
4. **The instance cap** — instances sit at 3, Cloud Run *recommends* more, and *refused for want of an instance* appears.
5. **Static files** — the web service's CPU or latency rises while the backend is quiet.
6. **The database** — `/experiments/checks` slows while CPU is fine; connection latency or refusals rise.

Per-route data comes from the backend's own log line (`backend/staunlabor/request_log.py`) through the log-based metrics of `deploy/grafana/create-log-metrics.sh`; it starts when they are created. Set-up and costs: `deploy/grafana/README.md`.

panels.title: Requests per second
panels.description: Cloud Run's own count. Every visitor's request reaches the web service; only /api goes on to the backend.

panels.title: p95 latency, as Cloud Run measures it
panels.description: From the request reaching a running container until it leaves; startup is not included (see Cold starts).

panels.title: Refused or failed, per minute
panels.description: 429 and 5xx as the containers answered them (the budget's 429 included), and Cloud Run's own refusals for want of an instance, which never reach a container and are missing from Cloud Run's request count.

panels.title: 1 · CPU: one calculation at a time per backend instance (1 vCPU, one worker)
Backend CPU utilization across instances
panels.description: Cloud Run's distribution over the backend's instances. Cloud Run adds an instance at about 60 %, up to the cap of 3.

panels.title: Backend latency in the container
panels.description: Cloud Run's request latency for the backend: p50, p95, p99.

panels.title: Requests in flight per backend instance
panels.description: The most requests one active instance held at once in a minute. Above 1 with CPU near 100 %, calculations queue for the core inside the instance (up to 20 per instance, --concurrency).

panels.title: CPU used, by route (cores)
panels.description: Each request's CPU from the app's line, summed per route: 1.0 is one instance's whole core. Requests that overlap share the CPU of their overlap equally (request_log.CpuShares), so the stack adds up to what the backend used.

panels.title: p95 time in the app, by route
panels.description: From the request entering the app to the last byte handed to the server. Far above the route's CPU per call: it waited for the core.

panels.title: CPU per call, by route (mean over the range)
panels.description: What one call costs. Overlap moves CPU from dear calls to cheap ones in this figure, so read the true cost from a quiet hour.

panels.title: Requests per minute, by route and status
panels.description: From the app's line: every /api request the backend answered.

panels.title: Instances by state
panels.description: Cloud Run's instance count: active ones serve requests, idle ones wait to be reused or removed. The dashed line is the cap of 3.

panels.title: Container startup latency
panels.description: How long a new instance took to start (Cloud Run, beta metric). The backend imports the app first: about 4.4 s measured on 2026-11-13.

panels.title: Waiting before an instance takes the request
panels.description: Cloud Run's pending latency (beta): from the request reaching Cloud Run until an instance takes it, waiting for a free slot or a new instance's start.

panels.title: Cold requests, by route
panels.description: The first request each new backend process answered: which route met a fresh instance and paid the first-time work (the first database connection of /experiments/checks, the Chladni modes' one computation).

panels.title: Time in the app of cold requests, by route
panels.description: Their mean time in the app. The process's start (the import) comes before and is in the startup latency instead.

panels.title: 3 · The per-address budget: 90 calculations per 10 s, per instance
Refused by the budget, per minute, by route
panels.description: 429s the app answered itself: a per-address budget was spent (security.py, or the kit's windows on the account routes). Cloud Run's own 429 never reaches the app and is in row 4.

panels.title: Share of API requests the budget refused
panels.description: Refusals rising while CPU is fine point to visitors sharing an address. The line names no address, by design.

panels.title: 4 · The instance cap: at most 3 instances per service
Instances against the cap
panels.description: All instances of each service, idle ones included. At 3 a service cannot grow.

panels.title: Instances Cloud Run recommends
panels.description: What Cloud Run's autoscaler would like, and what drives it. Above the cap of 3 the cap is in the way.

panels.title: Refused for want of an instance, per minute
panels.description: Cloud Run's own answers when no instance could take a request: 429 at the cap, 500 when traffic rose faster than it could scale. Counted from Cloud Run's request log (create-log-metrics.sh).

panels.title: Web CPU utilization across instances
panels.description: Caddy serves the files and proxies /api.

panels.title: Web latency in the container
panels.description: Includes the /api requests it proxies, which wait for the backend: compare the backend's latency in row 1.

panels.title: Bytes sent per second
panels.description: What the web service sends (to visitors: internet) and, for comparison, what the backend sends to it (the API's answers, part of the web's own).

panels.title: Web requests per second: files and pages against /api
panels.description: Files and pages are the web's requests less the backend's.

panels.title: Web responses by class, per second
panels.description: Cloud Run's response classes for the web service.

panels.title: 6 · The database: /experiments/checks (pool 1 + 1, shared Cloud SQL instance)
/experiments/checks: time in the app
panels.description: The one exhibit route that reads the database: once a minute per instance (exhibit_checks.LIST_TTL_S), every other call answers from the process. A slow p95 with a fast p50 is that one read.

panels.title: Backend → Cloud SQL: connection latency
panels.description: Cloud Run's measure of the backend's connections to Cloud SQL.

panels.title: Backend → Cloud SQL: connections per minute
panels.description: Connections the backend opened, and those refused.

panels.title: Connections to the database staunlabor, by state
panels.description: Needs the monitoring.viewer grant in the project keksdose (README, step 4). The pool's ceiling at three instances is six (dashed); the app role's own limit is twelve.

panels.title: Shared instance CPU (keksdose-db)
panels.description: Every app on the shared instance counts here. Needs the same grant.
